_about: Text for the scenes at places (data/events/setpieces.json). Keys ending @english or @dutch are the side's version.
event.grahamstown_bible.body: A crowd has gathered outside Graham's Town where Piet Uys's people are camped with their wagons. The English settlers have brought a gift: a great Dutch Bible, bound in leather, to send with the trekkers into the north. Speeches are made in English and in Dutch.
event.grahamstown_bible.body@english: A crowd has gathered outside Graham's Town where Piet Uys's people are camped with their wagons. Your neighbours, the English settlers, have brought a gift: a great Dutch Bible, bound in leather, to send with the trekkers into the north. Mr Philipps speaks, and the trekkers listen with their hats in their hands.
event.grahamstown_bible.attend: Join the crowd and hear the speeches
event.grahamstown_bible.attend.done: The Bible is handed over, and old Uys thanks the settlers. For one afternoon English and Dutch stand together on the veld. Your family leaves for the wagons in good spirits.
event.grahamstown_bible.talk: Talk with the Uys people about the road north
event.grahamstown_bible.talk.done: Some of the trekkers are surprised that an English family means to go north as well. They are friendly enough today. You learn the names of a few families, and they learn yours.
event.grahamstown_bible.prepare: Stay with the wagons and get ready
event.grahamstown_bible.prepare.done: While the town is busy at the gathering, you grease the axles, check the yokes, and let the oxen graze.
event.colesberg_edge.body: Colesberg sits at the very edge of the Colony. Men in the street talk of nothing but the trek: who has gone, who is going, and whether the Governor will try to stop them. The magistrate says that, under the new Punishment Act, the King's law follows his subjects even beyond the Orange.
event.colesberg_edge.ask_road: Ask about the [[drifts]] on the Orange
event.colesberg_edge.ask_road.done: A transport rider tells you which drift is best at this time of year and how to read the water.
event.colesberg_edge.letter: Write a last letter to send back down the road
event.colesberg_edge.letter.done: Everyone adds a line, and the children draw pictures in the margin. The letter goes south with a wagon tomorrow.
event.colesberg_edge.magistrate: Hear what the magistrate has to say
event.colesberg_edge.magistrate.done: The magistrate is polite. He has no orders to stop anyone. He only wants it known that the law still holds beyond the Orange.
event.philippolis_arrival.body: Philippolis is a Griqua town of houses, gardens and a church. Horsemen ride in to see who has come. They speak Dutch as well as you do, and they want to know what all these wagons mean for their land.
event.philippolis_arrival.respects: Go and pay your respects to the Griqua leaders
event.philippolis_arrival.respects.done: You are received with some caution, but courteously. They tell you that all who pass are welcome, so long as they pass.
event.philippolis_arrival.news: Ask what news there is from the north
event.philippolis_arrival.news.done: Griqua riders were with the commando at Mosega in January. They tell of the battle at Vegkop last year, and of Moroka's help to the trekkers afterwards.
event.stormberg_pass.body: The road climbs into the Stormberg. The track is steep and stony, and a cold wind comes down off the heights. Ahead, the climb gets steeper still.
event.stormberg_pass.double: Double the span on the steep pitches (half a day)
event.stormberg_pass.double.done: You take the steep pitches with a double span, unyoking and walking the oxen back down for each one. It is slow, but the wagon goes up safely.
event.stormberg_pass.push.ok: {speaker} picks the line, and the oxen haul the wagon over the top without trouble.
event.stormberg_pass.push.bad: Near the top the wagon slips back onto a rock. The axle takes the blow.
event.buffelsvlei_news.body: At Buffelsvlei a farmer's family is camped by the drift, waiting for their own people. Retief's party crossed here in March, they say: many wagons, with herds that took a whole day to cross.
event.buffelsvlei_news.listen: Sit with them and hear the news
event.buffelsvlei_news.listen.done: They talk late into the night about Retief, about the land beyond, and about the families still to come. It is good to know you are not alone on this road.
event.buffelsvlei_news.go: Thank them and make ready to cross
event.buffelsvlei_news.go.done: You wish them well and go down to look at the river.
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.body: Thaba Nchu is the largest town you have seen since the Colony: hundreds of round houses below the Black Mountain, with the mission church among them. This is the town of Moroka, chief of the Barolong. Last year, after the fight at Vegkop, he sent oxen to bring Potgieter's stranded families here. Trekker wagons are camped all around.
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.respects: Go to pay your respects to Moroka
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.respects.done: Moroka receives you with his councillors around him. Through an interpreter he asks where you are going, and how long the wagons mean to stay in this country.
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.gift: It is the custom to bring a gift. What will you offer?
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.gift.none: You have nothing suitable to give
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.gift.thanks: The gift is accepted with thanks. You leave with Moroka's good will.
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.gift.none.done: You apologise. Moroka says nothing about it, but the councillors look at one another.
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.mission.done: The missionaries ask about the road and give you medicine from their stores. They worry about what so many wagons will mean for the Barolong.
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.trekkers: Go among the trekker camps for news
event.thaba_nchu_moroka.trekkers.done: Families who were at Vegkop tell you about the battle: the laager of wagons, the long day, and the cattle driven away afterwards. Without Moroka's oxen they could not have moved.
event.sand_river_laager.body: By the Sand River the trekker parties have gathered into one great [[laager]]. Leaders are being chosen, and men argue loudly over where the trek should go next: north over the Vaal, or east over the mountains to Natal.
event.sand_river_laager.body@english: By the Sand River the trekker parties have gathered into one great laager. Heads turn as your wagon comes in. An English family here is something new, and not everyone is pleased.
event.sand_river_laager.join: Join the laager and take your place in the council
event.sand_river_laager.join.done: You draw your wagon into the ring, and that night {head} is welcomed at the council fire. You are among your own people.
event.sand_river_laager.ask: Ask to bring your wagon into the laager
event.sand_river_laager.ask.done: Word of how you helped trekker families on the road has gone ahead of you. After some talk, a place is made in the ring for your wagon. You have earned your welcome.
event.sand_river_laager.outside.done: You outspan a short way off. Before long an old trekker walks over to your fire.
event.sand_river_laager.question: "So, you are going north with us. Tell me plainly: are you the Governor's man?"
event.sand_river_laager.question.honest: "No. We are a family looking for land, like you."
He looks at you a long while, then nods. "We shall see," he says. It is a start.
event.sand_river_laager.question.help: Offer gunpowder for the laager's defence (4 lb)
event.sand_river_laager.question.help.do: He weighs the powder bag in his hand. "That is a neighbour's gift," he says, and shakes your hand.
event.sand_river_laager.question.leave: Say nothing and keep to yourselves
event.sand_river_laager.question.leave.d: He shrugs and goes back to the laager. You keep your own counsel and your own guard.
event.vaal_news.body: At the Vaal drift you meet a Barolong herder watering cattle. He has heard what happened at Mosega in January: the trekker commando and its allies attacked, the town was destroyed, and thousands of cattle were driven away. The Ndebele have gone north, he says, out of reach.
event.vaal_news.listen: Ask him what it was like for the people at Mosega
event.vaal_news.listen.done: He speaks quietly of families who lost their homes and herds there, and of the Ndebele moving north to find new land. Others, he says, will come to this country now. He asks whether your people mean to stay. You do not know what to tell him.
event.vaal_news.cross.done: You thank him and turn your eyes to the river.
event.mooi_arrival.body: The Mooi River. It means 'the pretty river', and it is: clear water over stones, willows, and good grass on both banks. Other wagons have already come. Smoke rises from Barolong and Bahurutshe homesteads in the distance. This is where your family means to stay.
event.mooi_arrival.unyoke: Unyoke the oxen for the last time
event.mooi_arrival.unyoke.done: The oxen walk stiffly down to the water and drink. The children run along the bank. You have come a very long way.
